extracted.intended_audience: general literate English reading public interested in morals, manners, religion, and domestic conduct (early 18th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Short moral and social essays prescribing norms of religious behaviour, household management, sexual responsibility, modesty, and public manners addressed to the reading public. Contains prescriptive statements and illustrative letters exposing social vices and proper conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper devotion with reason and prudence
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Devotion itself may disorder the Mind unless its heats are tempered with Caution and Prudence; we should be particularly careful to keep our Reason as cool as possible, and to guard ourselves in all Parts of Life against the Influence of Passion, Imagination, and Constitution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fervours of Devotion, however well-intended, can lead to disorder; therefore religious feeling must be checked by reason and prudence to avoid mental disturbance and error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Enthusiasm (unchecked religious fervour)
rubrics_metrics.description: Devotion, when it does not lie under the Check of Reason, is very apt to degenerate into Enthusiasm: the Mind, inflamed with Devotions, is too much inclined to think they are blown up by something Divine, and may at last fling itself into imaginary Raptures and Extasies and slight Human Ordinances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a person imagines divine impulse and humours passion, they may refuse established forms of religion; thus one must prevent devotion from becoming ecstatic enthusiasm that rejects human ordinances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid Superstition and excess of religious ceremony
rubrics_metrics.description: Superstition is the Excess not only of Devotion, but of Religion in general: absurd habits or ceremonies once admitted into the Church stick in it forever and often degenerate into empty show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be wary of adopting novel or ridiculous rites and accoutrements in religious practice; ceremonial additions tend to persist and hollow out true religion. Examples include bishops' accoutrements and lengthy ceremonial actions that obscure substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value steady piety over enthusiasm or superstition
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing is so glorious in the Eyes of Mankind... as a strong, steady masculine Piety; but Enthusiasm and Superstition are the Weaknesses of human Reason, that expose us to the Scorn and Derision of Infidels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steady, rational piety confers genuine moral advantage; excesses of passion or ritual bring ridicule and degrade human reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status must be supported by merit and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatever Advantages of Fortune, Birth, or any other Good people possess above the rest of the World, they should show collateral Eminences besides those Distinctions; otherwise those Distinctions will avail only to keep up common Decencies and Ceremonies, not real favor or esteem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Birth or fortune alone do not secure esteem; those of higher station must exhibit prudence, equal behaviour, courage, activity, and other virtues to be truly respected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household leadership requires prudence, equal behaviour, and protection of dependants
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not only paying Wages, and giving Commands, that constitutes a Master of a Family; but Prudence, equal Behaviour, with Readiness to protect and cherish them, is what entitles a Man to that Character in their very Hearts and Sentiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good masters exercise justice, protect and cherish servants and family; reliance on fear alone produces only outward compliance, not true loyalty or virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not impose unsolicited advice (voluntary counsellors are presumptuous)
rubrics_metrics.description: To give any Body Advice, is to say to that Person, I am your Betters. Voluntary counsellors (the eternal Flirt and Disturber who is always visiting) disturb families by advising without being called.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsolicited advice intrudes on autonomy and rank; those who habitually offer advice unasked may be harmful to domestic peace and social relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority figures must command their hastiness and control passion
rubrics_metrics.description: He who is passionate, and takes no Care to command his Hastiness, does more Injury to his Friends and Servants in one half Hour, than whole Years can atone for.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passionate indiscretion produces far more mischief in conversation and domestic life than ill-nature; those in authority should govern their tempers to avoid harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid employing 'spies' in households; they breed jealousy and disorder
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Spy is entertained, the Peace of that House is from that Moment banished. Spies never give an Account of good Services, but represent Mirth and Freedom as Wantonness and Disorder; masters become Cyphers in their own Families and live in continual Suspicion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrusting household oversight to informers undermines trust, fosters misunderstanding, and hands management to false and perfidious agents; household heads should avoid such practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fathers and men who cause illegitimate births owe duty of provision and education
rubrics_metrics.description: Men who propagate children by indirect methods should take care of those unfortunate creatures and give their spurious Children such an Education as may render them more virtuous than their Parents; they are bound in common Humanity and by Religion to make some Provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rather than leaving shame and neglect to illegitimate offspring, fathers should provide support and education as atonement; social notions that transfer the stigma solely onto the innocent are unjust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expose and guard against pandars and false representatives who harm reputations
rubrics_metrics.description: There are Prostitutes who, by persuading vain young fellows and writing letters in the name of Women of Figure, raise money and reputations falsely, thereby prostituting a Lady by proxy and injuring reputations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public exposure of such practices is justified to protect the reputations of honourable women and to deter those who would defame by false representations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congregational singing must conform; theatrical individuality in public worship is schismatic
rubrics_metrics.description: Singing the Psalms in a different Tune from the rest of the Congregation is a Sort of Schism not tolerated by that Act; theatrical manner of singing (introducing Italian airs and divisions) makes the parish ridiculous and infects others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public worship requires unity of practice; flamboyant, individualistic singing undermines devotion and should be restrained as contrary to the toleration claimed by the singer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice modesty and self-denial; avoid overclaiming merit
rubrics_metrics.description: Those who by their Words and Actions take as much upon themselves as they can barely demand in the strict Scrutiny of their Deserts will find their account lessen every Day. A modest Man preserves his Character, as a frugal Man does his Fortune.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep desires, words, and actions within the regard you observe from friends; self-denial and modesty often bring unexpected blessings and preserve reputation.
